jev.group.help: Check and use the built-in JEV client.
jev.status.help: Show the JEV provider, client, key source and endpoint (no network call, no key printed).
jev.ask.help: Ask JEV typed questions about a state and print the answers.
jev.batch.help: Ask JEV the same questions about many items (JSONL) and write one answer line per item.
jev.arg.questions: JSON file with the questions object.
jev.arg.state: The state text to ask about.
jev.arg.state_file: File with the state text to ask about.
jev.arg.items: JSONL file with one {"id", "state"} object per line.
jev.arg.out: JSONL file to write, one line per item, in input order.
jev.error.item_shape: each line must be an object with a string "id" and a string "state"
jev.error.item_duplicate_id: the id {id} was already used on an earlier line
jev.error.no_items: the items file {path} has no items
jev.key.help: Manage the JEV API key in your per-user key file.
jev.key.set.help: Read the JEV API key from stdin (one line) and store it in your per-user key file (0600); the key is never printed.
jev.error.key_stdin_tty: stdin is a terminal; pipe the key in instead, for example from your password manager, so it is not echoed or kept in your shell history
